transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really scared because for the past two months, I've felt like I'm constantly being watched and monitored. I've also been hearing these voices when no one is around, and I don't know who to trust anymore. It feels like everyone is targeting me.

I'm so sorry you've been going through that. Alongside these scary experiences, have you noticed any major changes in your mood, such as feeling extremely down and depressed, or unusually energetic and high?
No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. I don't feel unusually energetic or deeply depressed. I'm just mostly scared and anxious because of everything that's happening to me.
Before these past two months, had you ever experienced similar episodes, or noticed any gradual changes in your ability to work, socialize, or take care of yourself?

Looking back, I think I've been struggling for about a year and nine months in total. Long before these scary experiences started two months ago, I began pulling away from my friends and found it really hard to manage my daily responsibilities. It just gradually got worse over that time.

No, I don't use any recreational drugs or drink alcohol at all. I also haven't started taking any new medications recently. Everything I've been experiencing has just been happening on its own.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past, or have you recently had any physical health issues or head injuries?
No, I've never been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past. I haven't had any recent physical health issues or any head injuries either.
Could you tell me a bit more about the voices you hear? For example, do they talk to you directly, or do they seem to be talking to each other about you?

It actually varies quite a bit. Sometimes they talk directly to me, but other times they just whisper about me in the background. It is incredibly distracting and distressing to hear them all the time.
Along with pulling away from others, have you felt emotionally flat or empty, or found it difficult to organize your thoughts when trying to speak?

I don't really feel emotionally flat or empty, but I definitely have a very hard time organizing my thoughts when I try to speak. I find myself constantly jumping from one topic to another without any real connection, or I'll just completely lose track of what I was saying mid-sentence.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with a 21-month history of symptoms, starting with a 19-month prodromal phase of social withdrawal and functional decline, followed by 2 months of active psychotic symptoms including persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, and disorganized speech (formal thought disorder). There is no history of major mood episodes (ruling out Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Disorder, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features) and no substance or medical etiology. The presence of prominent hallucinations and disorganized speech rules out Delusional Disorder. This clinical picture and timeline (total duration > 6 months, active phase > 1 month) meet the DSM-5 criteria for Schizophrenia.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with persecutory delusions ('constantly being watched', 'everyone is targeting me') and auditory hallucinations ('hearing these voices') lasting for the past two months. This presentation suggests a psychotic process. The differential diagnosis includes primary psychotic disorders such as Schizophrenia and Delusional Disorder (though the latter is less likely due to prominent auditory hallucinations), as well as mood disorders with psychotic features (Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features) and Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar or Depressive Type). Further history regarding mood episodes is required to narrow this down.
